items.title: Periodic fluid Fourier Sobolev spaces
items.statement: For an integer $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ carry the probability measure obtained by pushing normalized Haar measure on $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$ forward under $y\mapsto x=2\pi y$; in coordinates this is $(2\pi)^{-d}dx$, and the characters are $e_k(x)=e^{ik\cdot x}$. For $q:Q_d\to\mathbb R^N$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, set $\widehat q(k)=\int_{Q_d}q(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$, componentwise, so real fields have $\widehat q(-k)=\overline{\widehat q(k)}$. Put $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$. For any $s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(Q_d;\mathbb R^N)$ as the completion of finite real trigonometric polynomials in the norm $\|q\|_{H^s}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2s}|\widehat q(k)|^2$. The completion is identified with its weighted coefficient space using finite symmetric cutoffs. If $s\ge0$, it has a unique $L^2$ representative; for $s<0$ no $L^2$ representative is asserted.
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.

items.title: Projected no-slip Stokes Hilbert space
items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $R>0$, and let $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^d$ be a nonempty bounded open set. Define $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ as the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ in the real $W^{1,2}$ norm. Define $\operatorname{div}v=0$ distributionally to mean $\int_\Omega v\cdot
abla\phi=0$ for every $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, and set $V=\{v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d):\operatorname{div}v=0\}$. Equip $V$ with the inherited $H^1$ inner product $\int_\Omega(v\cdot w+
abla v:
abla w)$. The phrase no-slip here means membership in this closure; no trace characterization on arbitrary $\Omega$ is part of the definition.

items.title: Rectangular continuous divergence inverse on mean-zero tests
items.statement: Let $d\ge1$ and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^d(a_i,b_i)$ be a nonempty finite open rectangle. Write $D(\Omega)=C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and $D_0(\Omega)=\{h\in D(\Omega):\int_\Omega h=0\}$. For every compact $K\subset\Omega$ there is a compact $K'\subset\Omega$ such that a linear map $R:D_0(\Omega)\to D(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ sends tests supported in $K$ to fields supported in $K'$, satisfies $\operatorname{div}(Rh)=h$, and is continuous on each fixed-support test space for the seminorms $\sup|\partial^\alpha h|$.
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.

items.title: Periodic Fourier embeddings and products
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ and use $H^\sigma(Q_d)$ with the normalized measure and weights in the Definition. For every integer $j\ge0$ and $\sigma>j+d/2$, each scalar $q\in H^\sigma(Q_d)$ has a $C^j$ representative and $\|q\|_{C^j}\le C_{d,\sigma,j}\|q\|_{H^\sigma}$. For every $\sigma>d/2$, pointwise multiplication extends uniquely from trigonometric polynomials to a continuous bilinear map $H^\sigma\times H^\sigma\to H^\sigma$ satisfying $\|fg\|_{H^\sigma}\le C_{d,\sigma}\|f\|_{H^\sigma}\|g\|_{H^\sigma}$. The assertions extend componentwise to finite-dimensional vector and tensor fields.

items.title: Periodic Leray and pressure maps
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and fix $d\in\{1,2,3\}$. For a vector Fourier coefficient $a(k)\in\mathbb C^d$, define $(Pa)(0)=a(0)$ and $(Pa)(k)=P_ka(k)$ for $k
e0$, where $P_k=I-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2$. For a tensor field $F=(F_{ij})_{i,j=1}^d$ with coefficients in any $H^s(Q_d)$, define the scalar pressure map $Q$ by $\widehat{QF}(0)=0$ and $\widehat{QF}(k)=-\sum_{i,j=1}^d k_i k_j|k|^{-2}\widehat F_{ij}(k)$ for $k
e0$. These formulas define real-preserving bounded maps on every $H^s$, $s\in\mathbb R$; $P$ is an orthogonal projection and commutes with derivatives. With $(\operatorname{div}F)_i=\sum_j\partial_jF_{ij}$, they satisfy $
abla QF=-(I-P)\operatorname{div}F$ as Fourier distributions.

items.title: Tame transport commutator
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $m\ge s\ge4$ be integers, let $f,g\in C^\infty(Q_d;\mathbb R)$, and define $\Lambda^m$ by $\widehat{\Lambda^m q}(k)=w_k^m\widehat q(k)$. For each coordinate $j$,
$$\|[\Lambda^m,f]\partial_jg\|_{L^2}\le C_{d,m,s}\bigl(\|f\|_{H^m}\|g\|_{H^s}+\|f\|_{H^s}\|g\|_{H^m}\bigr),$$
where $[\Lambda^m,f]h=\Lambda^m(fh)-f\Lambda^mh$.

items.title: Pressure recovery for smooth periodic incompressible velocity
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $s>d/2+1$, and let $u\in H^s(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$ satisfy $\operatorname{div}u=0$ distributionally. Then $u\otimes u\in H^s$, the mean-zero scalar $\pi=Q(u\otimes u)$ belongs to $H^s$, and in $H^{s-1}$,
$$P(u\cdot
abla u)=u\cdot
abla u+
abla\pi.$$
Among mean-zero periodic distributions satisfying the identity, this pressure is unique. The formula is a torus pressure recovery result and asserts no wall pressure regularity.

items.title: Directional Poincaré bound for zero trace
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $d\ge2$, $R>0$, and let $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^d$ be bounded and open. For every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$,
$$\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le2R\|\partial_1v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le2R\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
Here $H_0^1$ is the closure of compactly supported smooth fields in the Sobolev norm.
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.

items.title: Projected stationary weak Stokes solvability
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $d\ge2$, let $R>0$, let $\Omega\subset(-R,R)^d$ be nonempty bounded open, let $\mu>0$, and let $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$. There is a unique $u\in V$ such that
$$\mu\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v=\int_\Omega f\cdot v\qquad(v\in V),$$
where $V$ is the distributionally divergence-free subspace of $H_0^1$ defined above. It satisfies $\|
abla u\|_2\le2R\|f\|_2/\mu$. This is a projected variational velocity result; it asserts no pressure, $L^2$ pressure regularity, or classical boundary regularity.

items.title: Difference energy for given smooth incompressible and symmetric solutions
items.statement:

abla z)=
u\Delta z$ on $Q_d$, with the same $
u\ge0$, then for $w=u-v$,
$$\|w(t)\|_2^2\le\|w(0)\|_2^2\exp\!\left(2\int_0^t\|
abla v(	au)\|_\infty d	auight).$$
(ii) If $q,r$ are already given smooth solutions of $z_t+\sum_{j=1}^dA_j(z)\partial_jz=0$ with each $A_j:\mathbb R^N	o\mathbb R^{N	imes N}$ a fixed linear map into symmetric matrices, then
$$\|q(t)-r(t)\|_2^2\le\|q(0)-r(0)\|_2^2\exp\!\left(C\int_0^t(\|
abla q\|_\infty+\|

In either case, if $s\ge1$ and both solution families have a common $H^s$ bound $M$ on $[0,T]$, then $\|w(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le (2M)^{(s-1)/s}\|w(0)\|_2^{1/s}e^{\Gamma t/(2s)}$, where $\Gamma$ is any uniform rate in the corresponding squared $L^2$ estimate. items.title: Rectangular no-slip Stokes velocity and distribution pressure
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^d(a_i,b_i)\subset(-R,R)^d$ be a nonempty finite rectangle, let $\mu>0$, and let $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$. The projected variational theorem gives a unique $u\in V$ with $\mu\int
abla u:
abla v=\int f\cdot v$ for all $v\in V$ and $\|
abla u\|_2\le2R\|f\|_2/\mu$. There is a distribution $p\in H^{-1}(\Omega):=(H_0^1(\Omega))'$ such that $-\mu\Delta u+
abla p=f$ in $D'(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$; it is unique modulo constant distributions. With the quotient norm on $H^{-1}/\mathbb R$, the map $f\mapsto(u,[p])$ is bounded and linear. The pressure is not asserted to lie in $L^2$ or to be smooth at rectangle corners.

title: Periodic fluid Fourier Sobolev spaces — Examples

items.title: Shear mode has zero periodic pressure
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $A\in\mathbb R$, and $u(x)=A\sin(x_2)e_1$ on $Q_d$, where $e_1$ is the first coordinate vector. Then $u$ is smooth and divergence-free, $u\cdot\nabla u=0$, and its unique mean-zero pressure recovered by $Q(u\otimes u)$ is $\pi=0$. This is a verification of the pressure recovery map; it is not asserted to solve an unforced viscous Navier–Stokes equation.

items.title: Full wall Stokes pressure requires a divergence inverse
items.statement: Assume full AC. The projected stationary Stokes theorem on a bounded open set establishes a unique variational velocity in the divergence-free $H_0^1$ space; its conclusion contains no pressure. The separate rectangular theorem uses a continuous right inverse of divergence on compactly supported mean-zero tests to construct a distribution pressure in $H^{-1}$, unique modulo constants, for finite rectangles. These results do not claim an $L^2$ pressure estimate or pressure recovery on arbitrary bounded open sets; such a claim requires an additional domain-appropriate divergence or inf-sup argument.
